metadata.description: read-heavy product recommendations: concurrent read scaling under a production-shaped read/write MIX (paired control vs mixed arms)

notes: METRIC PROVENANCE (rmp #805): storage.wal_bytes is the WAL bytes WRITTEN — graphus_wal_bytes_written_total (rmp #745), scraped from the co-located server /metrics — a MONOTONIC, reclamation-independent volume that is STABLE across identical runs (3-run spread 69,050,344..69,212,357 B = 0.23%), which is why it can gate a durability regression. It REPLACES the pre-#805 storage.wal_bytes, which was the on-disk WAL DIRECTORY size at teardown — a bimodal snapshot (the same configuration produced 1,871,597 and 31,457,384 B on repeat, a 17x spread) that gated nothing and masked regressions. The on-disk directory walk is now reported SEPARATELY as storage.wal_retained_bytes (still bimodal, kept for diagnostic interest, NOT gated). write_amplification/space_amplification use store + WAL-written and are therefore stable too. The pre-#805 committed baseline had wal_bytes=7,360,747 (a directory snapshot) and write_amplification=5.87 (computed from that snapshot); neither is comparable to these.

CONCURRENCY LADDER (read-heavy MIX, 8 rungs × 2 arm(s) over 1,2,4,8 against 'recodb'): the headline evidence is where throughput SATURATES while latency explodes and only a subset of cores stay busy — the single-engine-thread vs off-thread-reader-pool signature — measured under a PRODUCTION-SHAPED MIX (reads served while writes commit underneath), not against a frozen graph.

TWO LAYERS OF TRUTH, never conflated (rmp #714, #715). READ: throughput.* is ONE coherent set — the 1500 reads of the best 'mixed' rung (C=8), at 770.4 ops/s, and throughput.abort_rate = 0.000000 is the READ abort rate. It is a MEASURED zero, not a placeholder: a standalone auto-commit read runs at SNAPSHOT ISOLATION (rmp #543/#545), so it can neither abort a writer nor be aborted by one — that is invariant I1, and the run FAILS if a read ever aborts. WRITE: the writers' evidence lives in the workload map and is split in two. ENGINE: 0 of 1450 transaction attempts were aborted by SSI (engine_abort_rate 0.000000). APPLICATION: 1450 of 1450 business units COMMITTED (write_commit_rate 1.000000), at 0.0000 retries per commit, 0 exhausting their retry budget. A high engine abort rate WITH a full application commit rate is a HEALTHY system under contention: the application-visible cost of contention is LATENCY (see write_p99_ms, which is RETRY-INCLUSIVE), not lost work.

THE COST OF THE MIX (rmp #714). Every rung was run TWICE, back to back, same concurrency, same op budget, same graph: once with the writers OFF (the control) and once with them ON (the treatment — the production-shaped default this report headlines). What the mix costs the READ path: -4.9% at the best rung (C=8). Rung by rung: C=1: 247.9 → 217.7 ops/s (-12.2%), p99 27.0 → 26.4 ms | C=2: 424.7 → 378.5 ops/s (-10.9%), p99 34.0 → 33.4 ms | C=4: 699.9 → 619.1 ops/s (-11.5%), p99 40.5 → 45.7 ms | C=8: 810.3 → 770.4 ops/s (-4.9%), p99 81.8 → 80.0 ms. The control arm runs FIRST at every rung, so it warms the buffer pool for the mixed arm — the cost reported here is therefore a conservative LOWER BOUND. This is the number a capacity planner needs and that a read-only ladder against a frozen graph can never produce.

THE WRITE STREAM is production-shaped, not a storm: 2 writer(s) paced at one business unit every 20ms, each driven through MANAGED RETRY (bounded exponential backoff + jitter — what session.execute_write does in every official driver). 25% of the units are a read-modify-write of one of 4 TRENDING products (`SET p.hot = coalesce(p.hot,0)+1`); the rest CREATE a PURCHASED edge on a random (user, product) pair. The hot component is what makes SSI — and therefore the retry path — LOAD-BEARING: a purely random write stream conflicts with nobody, aborts nothing, and leaves the retry path as dead code and the bounded-retries invariant vacuous.

SLOW-READER PROBE (invariant I5, the GC pin — rmp #551): while 124 heavy 'r3_fof3' traversals (p50 23.6ms, max 40.6ms) held their MVCC snapshots open for 3.0s, the writers committed 240 of 240 business units underneath them (0 engine aborts). A long reader pins the GC watermark; if that pin could stall the write path, this window would show ZERO commits — and the ladder, whose reads are all short, would never have noticed.

storage.bytes_per_node / bytes_per_relationship are deliberately ABSENT (rmp #711/#714): the dataset counts are the GENERATOR's seed graph, while the mixed arm COMMITTED 1450 business unit(s) into this same store — most of them a CREATE of a new PURCHASED edge. The store therefore no longer holds the graph those counts describe, and a per-element cost computed from them would be real arithmetic over the wrong graph.

storage.* is the REAL footprint of the 'recodb' database after the ladder: a 6873088 B store image, plus 69180880 B written to the WAL (storage.wal_bytes = graphus_wal_bytes_written_total, the STABLE write volume) with 27341937 B still retained on disk in the WAL DIRECTORY at teardown (storage.wal_retained_bytes, a bimodal snapshot, NOT gated). The amplification ratios are store + WAL-written over the generator's 2437533 B logical CSV — and they now include the durable cost of the writes the mix committed, so they are an UPPER bound on the load's own amplification.
